editionData.description: Global headlines: Turkey’s LGBT crackdown draws international condemnation, protests (Turkish authorities have raided the offices of LGBT organizations and places frequented by the community); African IPO turns people into oil tycoons, and they have the memes to prove it (A minimum investment of $3.94 can buy a partnership with the continent’s richest man); and More U.S. troops have died amid Iran war than Pentagon has disclosed publicly (Officials who spoke with The Post expressed frustration that the additional loss of life in the Middle East is not reflected in the Defense Department’s casualty database). Markets leaned higher, with 4 of 7 tracked indexes up; Nikkei 225 up 1.38% was the largest move. Benchmarks tracked: S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, Euronext 100 Index, and Public Joint-Stock Company Moscow Exchange MICEX-RTS plus 3 more indexes. Hacker News: Human brain is two separate organs, Stanford Medicine-led research finds (Stanford Health Care delivers the highest levels of care and compassion. SHC treats cancer, heart disease, brain disorders, primary care...); San Francisco Onion Futures Company (The San Francisco Onion Futures Company offers private, transferable contracts for the future physical delivery of yellow onions); and If math is more than proof, we need to better celebrate the rest of it (terrytao.wordpress.com: If math is more than proof, we need to better celebrate the rest of it). Product Hunt features Bolt Forge (Bolt's new agent with open-source models and 50X usage), Steam Frame (Your Steam library, now on a wearable PC), and Mise (The meal planner that gets all your dishes ready at once).

headlines.summary: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

headlines.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
headlines.summary: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

headlines.title: US and Denmark reach deal to build US military presence in Greenland
headlines.summary: President Donald Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

headlines.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
headlines.summary: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

headlines.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
headlines.summary: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

headlines.title: Carney welcomes EU's associate membership
headlines.summary: BRUSSELS — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday welcomed a proposal for his country to become the European Union's first "associate member", shrugging off threats from US President Donald Trump.

headlines.title: Fed raises rate for 1st time since 2023
headlines.summary: The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate on Wednesday by a quarter of a percentage point, the first rise since 2023, as the central bank's new Chairman Kevin Warsh led a decisive move to tackle stubborn inflation, defying President Donald Trump's repeated calls for a rate cut.

headlines.title: Hostilities take heavy toll on Yemeni civilians: UN
headlines.summary: UNITED NATIONS - Hostilities spreading across Yemen are taking a devastating toll on struggling families, and relief agencies are ramping up aid for refugees arriving in Djibouti, UN humanitarians said on Thursday.

headlines.title: Jordan looks to cooperation with China on green energy
headlines.summary: China and Jordan have stepped up their efforts to deepen cooperation in fields such as green energy as the recent visit by Jordan's King Abdullah II to China opened new avenues for practical bilateral cooperation.

headlines.title: Sept 18 memories back in focus
headlines.summary: Friday marks the 95th anniversary of the September 18th Incident. Chinese and European political commentators and peace advocates have called for the lessons of history to be remembered amid mounting concerns over Japan's expanding military capabilities and a deteriorating regional security environment.

hackerNews.title: Science Is Open Software
hackerNews.summary: TL;DR I claim that modern science is synonymous with open source software. This post explains why, why it matters, and what you can (and should) do next. Why do you care about (open source) software? - Everyone I spend a lot of my time working on software. I have been asked why software matters more times than I can remember. Software is, people say, not science. It’s a time sink, something to rush past in the pursuit of what really matters: results (and papers if you’re in academia).
